rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says God will establish this mercy in the Hereafter for those who fear Him; this specifies the recipients after the verse's general wording and applies to those meeting the traits listed at the verse's end.
rows.anchor: يعني: فسأوجبها في الآخرة {للذين يتقون}، وهذا معنى قول المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those who fear as the community of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {للذين يتقون} (يريد: أمة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -)

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In one explanation, giving zakat means paying the alms due on one's wealth when their due time arrives.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: صدقات الأموال عند محلها)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second transmitted explanation takes giving zakat to mean obeying God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا عنه أنه قال في قوله: {ويؤتون الزكاة}: (يطيعون الله ورسوله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī understands this obedience as deeds that purify and cleanse the soul.
rows.anchor: كأنه ذهب إلى ما يزكي النفس ويطهرها من الأعمال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also interprets giving zakat here as obedience to God and His Messenger, understood as soul-purifying deeds.
rows.anchor: من الأعمال (¬9)، وبه # قال الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing in God's signs means affirming what He revealed to Muhammad and to the prophets before him.
rows.anchor: قال: (يريد: بما أنزلت (¬2) على محمد والنبيين قبله يصدقون)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say the Israelites asked for good in this world and the next and repented; God said His mercy encompassed all, then specified Muhammad's community for the promised mercy.
rows.anchor: فسألوه النعمة في الدنيا والآخرة، وتقربوا إليه بالتوبة من المعاصي

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The Israelites were among those encompassed by universal mercy, while Muhammad's community is singled out and promised it through the description of the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: فكانوا هم من جملة من وسعتهم الرحمة، ثم خص أمة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: نوف البكالي
rows.claim: Nawf al-Bikālī urges the listeners to praise a Lord who guarded their absence, secured their allotted share, and made Israel's delegation for them.
rows.anchor: ألا تحمدون ربا (¬6) حفظ غيبتكم وأخذ لكم بسهمكم (¬7)،

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says, through ʿAṭāʾ, that this delegation became the share of the righteous among Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: هذه الوفادة صارت للصالحين من أمة محمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās further identifies those who fear as Muhammad's community, the people who follow the unlettered Messenger and Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم زاد في البيان أن المراد # بقوله: {للذين يتقون} هذه الأمة، فقال: {الذين يتبعون الرسول النبي الأمي}

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: All the commentators define the unlettered prophet as one who neither writes nor reads.
rows.anchor: [والأمي] (¬1) الذي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ في قول جميع المفسرين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains ummī as remaining in the natural state of the community, never having learned scripture.
rows.anchor: معنى {الأمي}: الذي هو على خلقة الأمة، لم يتعلم الكتاب

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes his community as unlettered: it does not write or calculate.
rows.anchor: وقد قال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إنا أمة أمية لا نكتب ولا نحسب"

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses idh as accusative and supplies an imperative: remember when your Lord took the covenant.
rows.anchor: موضع {إذ} نصب، المعنى (¬3) واذكر {وإذ أخذ ربك}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats from their backs as an appositive clarifying from the children of Adam, meaning from the backs of Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: {من ظهورهم} بدل من قوله {من بني آدم}، والمعنى: وإذ أخذ ربك من ظهور بني آدم

rows.speaker: الكناني
rows.claim: Al-Kinānī says Adam's back is left unstated because all people are his descendants, extracted from his back through successive generations from one another.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر ظهر آدم، وإنما أخرجوا جميعا من ظهره؛ لأن الله تعالى أخرج ذرية آدم بعضهم من ظهور بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhurriyya is read in a plural form; its discussion was given under God's words about Abraham's offspring.
rows.anchor: وقرئ (¬3) {ذريتهم} جمعا، وقد ذكرنا معنى الذرية والكلام فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriyya can denote one person or a group, like bashar; this explains why a singular form can carry collective meaning without a plural ending.
rows.anchor: وبينا أن الذرية تقع على الواحد والجمع، فمن أفردها هاهنا فلأنه قد استغنى عن جمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unpluralized word bashar likewise applies to one or many, so the same usage accounts for an unpluralized dhurriyya.
rows.anchor: وكما لم يجمع (بشر) بتصحيح ولا تكسير كذلك لا تجمع الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who read dhurriyyāt argue that pluralizing is sound whether dhurriyya is singular or collective, just as broken plurals themselves can take a further plural.
rows.anchor: ومن جمع قال: إن الذرية إن كان واحدا فلا إشكال في جواز الجمع فيه

rows.speaker: مسلم بن يسار الجهني عن عمر
rows.claim: The first interpretation, held by commentators and traditionists, cites ʿUmar reporting the Prophet: God wiped Adam's back, extracted descendants, assigned some to Paradise and some to Hell, and each was made to do the corresponding people's deeds.
rows.anchor: مسلم (¬1) بن يسار الجهني: (أن عمر - رضي الله عنه - سئل عن هذه الآية فقال:

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's reported answer describes God creating Adam, wiping his back, extracting descendants, and assigning them to Paradise or Hell with deeds matching their destination.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سئل عنها فقال: "إن الله خلق آدم ثم مسح ظهره فاستخرج منه ذرية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked what deeds are for, the Prophet says God employs the person destined for Paradise in its people's deeds until death, and likewise the person destined for Hell in its people's deeds.
rows.anchor: فقال رجل: يا رسول الله ففيم العمل؟ فقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إن الله إذا خلق العبد للجنة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that when God created Adam and wiped his back, every descendant's soul to be created until the Resurrection fell from him; the source notes that the report continues at length.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "لما خلق الله آدم مسح على ظهره فسقط من ظهره

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God shook Adam and showed him all the descendants He had created through the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء في: قوله: {وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم} (يريد: نفض (¬3) آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God extracted Adam's descendants from his loins like tiny particles, asked who their Lord was, received their affirmation, then returned them to his loins until each was born without addition or loss.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: (إن الله خلق آدم ثم أخرج ذريته من صلبه مثل الذر

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says God gathered and formed them, made them speak, and took their covenant; He promised messengers and scriptures to remind them, and they confessed that He alone is God and Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: (جمعهم يومئذ، ثم صورهم، ثم استنطقهم وأخذ عليهم العهد والميثاق

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God struck Adam's back and brought out every soul destined for Paradise pure and white, and every soul destined for Hell black, as specks.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: (ضرب الله ظهر آدم فخرجت كل نفس مخلوقة للجنة بيضاء نقية

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Quraẓī says the spirits acknowledged faith and knowledge of God before their bodies were created.
rows.anchor: وقال القرظي: (أقر له بالإيمان والمعرفة الأرواح قبل أن يخلق أجسادها)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil describes white descendants drawn from Adam's right back and black ones from his left, the former promised Paradise by mercy and the latter Hell, before all were returned to Adam's loins until the covenant generations emerge from men and women.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (إن الله مسح صفحة ظهر آدم اليمنى فأخرج منه ذرية بيضاء كهيئة الذر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil links those who broke the first covenant to God's statement that He found most of them without a covenant.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى فيمن نقض العهد الأول: {وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد}

rows.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي وسعيد بن جبير وسعيد بن المسيب والضحاك وأبو صالح
rows.claim: The source says these authorities also hold the previously described extraction-of-descendants interpretation, identifying it as the position of the exegetes.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا قول عكرمة (¬3) والكلبي وسعيد بن جبير و [سعيد (¬4) بن المسيب] والضحاك (¬5) وأبي صالح

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows that God gave the tiny particles understanding, as in the speech of the ant and the mountains and birds glorifying with David.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون الله تعالى جعل لأمثال (¬7) الذر فهما يعقل به

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī attributes to hadith scholars and senior scholars the view that descendants emerged from Adam's and their fathers' loins as particles, accepted God's covenant with intellects implanted in them, as other creatures were made to understand speech or respond.
rows.anchor: مذهب أصحاب الحديث وكبراء أهل العلم في هذه الآية هو: أن الله عز وجل أخرج ذريات آدم

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of the نظم says the Prophet's report about extracting descendants from Adam does not conflict with the verse's mention of descendants' backs, since they descend from one another.
rows.anchor: ليس بين قول النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -:"إن الله مسح ظهر آدم فأخرج منه ذريته" و [بين] (¬2) الآية اختلاف

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The covenant establishes proof against every person, including those who did not reach maturity; adults also receive proof through signs, messengers, warnings, exhortations, and transmitted lessons.
rows.anchor: قد أثبت الحجة على كل منفوس ممن بلغ، وممن لم يبلغ بالميثاق الذي أخذه عليهم

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators say the blessed descendants acknowledged willingly while the wretched acknowledged under pressure, connecting this to submission by choice or compulsion.
rows.anchor: إن أهل السعادة من الذرية أقروا طوعا، وإن أهل الشقاوة أقروا تقية وكرها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says a child who dies young enters Paradise through knowledge of the first covenant, while a person reaching reason still must believe; the covenant remains proof against them.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: من مات صغيرا دخل الجنة بمعرفته بالميثاق (¬2) الأول، ومن بلغ العقل لم يغن عنه الميثاق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Muqātil's account represents the view that children of polytheists enter Paradise; those rejecting that outcome say the wretched acknowledged unwillingly, which did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره مذهب من يقول: إن أطفال المشركين يدخلون (¬4) الجنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the question Aren't I your Lord? as an affirmative demand that they acknowledge His lordship.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): (المعنى قال: {ألست بربكم} وهو إيجاب للإقرار عليهم بربوبيته)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their yes is an answer to God, affirming His lordship and their own servanthood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (هو جواب منهم له وإقرار له بالربوبية ولأنفسهم بالعبودية)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says that after the descendants acknowledged, God told the angels to bear witness, and the words We have witnessed record that command.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: (8) (لما أقروا، قال الله للملائكة: اشهدوا. فقال: {شهدنا})

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says the angels declared that they witnessed the descendants' acknowledgment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (قالت (¬3) الملائكة: شهدنا على إقراركم)

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī takes the verse as God's report that He and His angels witnessed Adam's descendants acknowledge Him.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: (هذا خبر من الله تعالى عن نفسه وملائكته أنهم شهدوا على إقرار بني آدم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On these interpretations, pausing after their yes is appropriate because the descendants' speech has ended.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذه الأقوال (¬6) يحسن الوقف على قوله: {بلى}؛ لأن كلام الذرية قد انقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan analysis attaches lest you say to We have witnessed, supplying the omitted negative particle; the example from al-Quṭāmī means lest it be sold.
rows.anchor: أي شهدنا عليهم بالإقرار لئلا تقولوا، فأسقط (لا) (¬7)

rows.speaker: القطامي
rows.claim: Al-Quṭāmī's line uses the construction with an understood not: its phrase means that it should not be sold.
rows.anchor: رأينا ما يرى البصراء فيها ... فآلينا عليها أن تباعا (¬9)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran analysis instead supplies an omitted noun: they witnessed from aversion to your saying this, rather than omitting la.
rows.anchor: وعند البصريين المحذوف مضاف بتقدير: شهدنا كراهة أن تقولوا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr also allows attaching lest you say to He made them testify; he calls this clearer and says the pause after We have witnessed is then invalid.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تعلق {أن} ب (أشهدهم) وهذا أوضح في التأويل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Some take We have witnessed as the descendants' own words, meaning they testified about themselves; on this view it does not attach to their yes, but lest you say attaches to He made them testify.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: قوله: {شهدنا} من كلام الذرية، والمعنى: شهدنا على أنفسنا بهذا الإقرار

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of the نظم gives another view: the covenant story ends at their yes, then God begins a report of what the polytheists will say at Judgment, with We have witnessed meaning We testify.
rows.anchor: وذكر صاحب النظم] (¬3) وجها آخر في قوله: {شهدنا} عن بعضهم

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: On the نظم author's alternative, We testify anticipates the polytheists' Judgment-day words; the covenant passage concerns all creatures, while the following story singles out polytheists.
rows.anchor: شهد الخطيئة حين يلقى ربه (¬5) # أي: يشهد، فيكون تأويله نشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads both lest you say and or you say with third-person yāʾ because the preceding wording speaks about them; the other readers use second-person tāʾ because the passage has shifted to direct address. Both are sound.
rows.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله: {أن تقولوا} [الأعراف:172]، {أو تقولوا} [الأعراف: 173]، فقرأ (¬3) أبو عمرو بالياء (¬4) جميعا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators call the covenant a reminder and proof for all morally responsible people, preventing unbelievers from claiming they were unaware of it.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هذه (¬7) الآية تذكير بما أخذ على جميع المكلفين من الميثاق، واحتجاج عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting the covenant does not invalidate the proof once God has disclosed it through a miracle-bearing Messenger; a truthful report stands in the mind as recollection.
rows.anchor: نسيانهم لذلك لا يسقط الاحتجاج بعد أن أخبر الله تعالى عن أخذ ذلك عليهم على لسان صاحب المعجزة

rows.speaker: عوف
rows.claim: ʿAwf says people will remember the covenant on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال عوف (¬3): (وسيذكرون الميثاق يوم القيامة)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say the covenant removes the excuse that people merely followed idolatrous ancestors while young and unaware; God cannot punish descendants for their parents' shirk because each person was bound to affirm monotheism. They connect the excuse to the claim about finding ancestors on a religious way.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هذا قطع لعذر الكفار فلا يستطيع أحد من الذرية أن يقول يوم القيامة:

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq offers a rationalist reading: God brought people from one another's backs, and their being made to testify means every adult can know God's oneness from the evidence of creation.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: (وقال بعضهم: إن الله عز وجل أخرج بني آدم بعضهم من ظهور بعض

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains that people effectively testify to God's lordship because signs and proofs compel them to recognize the Creator, even if they do not explicitly speak.
rows.anchor: وشرح أبو بكر هذا فقال: {وإذ أخذ ربك من} ذريات (¬3) {بني آدم من ظهورهم} أي: أخرجهم وأنشأهم بعد أن كانوا نطفا في أصلاب الآباء

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: He compares this figurative testimony to people being described as witnesses to their disbelief and to a person saying his limbs testified to another's statement, meaning they recognized it and would testify if able to speak.
rows.anchor: كما قال في غير هذا الموضع: {شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر} [التوبة: 17]، يريد: هم بمنزلة الشاهدين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī also reads God's testimony that there is no deity but Him as His informing and clarifying it, analogous to testimony before judges.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب أيضا {شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو} [آل عمران: 18] , # يريد: أعلم وبين

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that their hearts do not grasp reward or fear punishment.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: لا يعقلون بها ثوابا ولا يخافون عقابا)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says their hearts do not comprehend what is good or the path of guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (لا يعقلون بها الخير والهدى)

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains that their eyes do not see the path of guidance and right conduct.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: (يريد: سبيل الهدى والرشاد)

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says their ears fail to hear God's admonitions and the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال: (يريد مواعظ الله والقرآن)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says their perceptions are sealed, citing the statement that God sealed their hearts; hence their hearts do not understand, eyes do not see, and ears do not hear.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ({لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها} الآية. يقول الله تعالى: {ختم الله على قلوبهم}

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning say perception is denied because these people turn away as if unable to perceive; by rejecting truth they act like people who cannot understand, see, or hear.
rows.anchor: إنما نفى عنهم الإدراكات لأنهم يعرضون في جميع ذلك إعراض من لا يدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls the verse an explicit refutation of the Qadariyya: God created many humans and jinn for Hell, those whose primordial decree fixed their wretchedness, and they cannot escape their destination.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية صريح في الرد على القدرية؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكر أنه خلق كثيرا من الإنس والجن للنار

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they resemble cattle in eating and drinking.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: (شبههم بالأنعام في المأكل والمشرب)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they eat and drink without attending to the Hereafter, like cattle concerned only with eating; cattle hear without reasoning, as do these disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (يأكلون ويشربون لا يلتفتون إلى الآخرة كما تأكل الأنعام وتشرب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says cattle know their Lord and guard against ruin, making these people more astray.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: (يريد (¬4) إن الأنعام تعرف ربها وتحذر الهلاك)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says cattle obey God, whereas the unbeliever does not.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (لأن الأنعام مطيعة لله، والكافر (¬6) غير مطيع لله)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says cattle know and remember their Lord, while these people neither know nor remember Him, so their path is worse.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: (هم أخطأ طريقا من الأنعام؛ لأن الأنعام تعرف ربها وتذكره

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says cattle perceive benefits and harms and heed some of them, while most of these people knowingly defy God and proceed toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق في قوله: {بل هم أضل}: (وذلك أن الأنعام تبصر منافعها ومضارها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies the people described here as the disbelievers of Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: (يعني: كفار مكة)

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the heedless are unaware of the reward prepared for God's allies and the punishment prepared for His enemies.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: (عما أعد الله لأوليائه (¬2) من الثواب، وما أعد لأعدائه من العقاب)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they are heedless of the Hereafter and the punishment it contains.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (عن أمر الآخرة، وما فيها من العذاب)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators cite Abū Hurayra's report from the Prophet that God has ninety-nine names, one short of a hundred; the revealed names are bounded and known through religious authority, as indicated by the definite wording.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هي ما ذكره أبو هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "إن لله تبارك وتعالى تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة غير واحدة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling upon God by these names means honoring Him through invocation such as O Powerful, O Knowing, and O Generous.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فادعوه بها}؛ دعاؤه بها تعظيمه بذكرها؛ كقولك: يا قدير يا عليم يا كريم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says one should not call God by a name or attribute He did not use of Himself, such as generous, gentle, or strong-bodied, even when the proposed word is offered as a synonym.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬1): إلا ينبغي أنا تدعوه بما لم يصف به نفسه أو لم يسم به نفسه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another authority says one of the best forms of supplication is to invoke God by His beautiful names, as He commands here.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: (في هذه الآية دليل على أن من أفضل الدعاء أن تدعوا الله بالأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads yalḥidūn; ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī agree with this form in al-Naḥl, and al-Farrāʾ treats yalḥidūn and yalḥadūn as two language forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ (¬3) حمزة: {يلحدون}، ووافقه عاصم (¬4) والكسائي في النحل

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The lexicographers define ilḥād as turning away from the proper course.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة (¬1): (معنى الإلحاد في اللغة: الميل عن القصد)

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt defines a heretic as one who deviates from truth and inserts into religion what does not belong there.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: (الملحد العادل عن الحق المدخل فيه ما ليس فيه

rows.speaker: غيره من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Other lexicographers define it as deviation from uprightness and connect it with the side niche of a grave, unlike a central trench.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل اللغة: (الإلحاد العدل عن الاستقامة والانحراف عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the common reading, supported by the Qur'anic use of ilḥād in the sanctuary; ilḥād is more common in Arabic, and reading both forms can encompass both language variants.
rows.anchor: والأجود قراءة العامة؛ لقوله تعالى: {ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد} [الحج: 25]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify the people who deviate in God's names as polytheists who applied divine names to idols, altering them or deriving al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt from God's names.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد (¬2): ({الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} هم المشركون، عدلوا بأسماء الله عما هي عليه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning define them as those who call God by names He did not give Himself in scripture or through a Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (الذين يلحدون في أسماء الله الذين (¬3) يسمون الله بما لم يسم به نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses deviation in God's names as lying.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال: ({يلحدون في أسمائه} أي: يكذبون)

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says they turn away from the truth.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: (يميلون عن الحق)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī concludes that anyone assigning God a name without revealed authorization lies in that naming and departs from truth.
rows.anchor: فكل من سمى الله بما لم يرد به توقيف فقد كذب في ذلك (¬2) التسمية ومال عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deviate in God's names will receive in the Hereafter recompense for the deeds they used to do.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون} أي: جزاء ما كانوا يعملون في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives two parses for that God is not unjust: accusative after an implied and because, if that is accusative; or nominative as a continuation meaning that is because God, if that is nominative.
rows.anchor: في محل (أن) وجهان: أحدهما: النصب، بمعنى: وبأن الله، قال الفراء:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the people had been shown guidance, knew the right path, delayed migration, and doubted God's power and support for His Messenger; thus their punishment was deserved for prior disbelief and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: تبين سبيل (¬6) الهدى، وعرفتم سبيل الرشاد، وتربصتم عن الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the denial of injustice begins a new sentence, not a cause of punishment: their deeds caused punishment, while this clause describes its justice. He therefore prefers a nominative parse; al-Kisāʾī also allows beginning a sentence with the clause.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن قوله: {وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد} ابتداء كلام لا يعود معناه إلى ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that creating acts and then punishing for them would make God unjust, Al-Wāḥidī answers that God may dispose of His own dominion as He wills; injustice cannot be attributed to its owner.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن له أن يتصرف في ملكه بما يشاء، ومن كان له أن يتصرف في ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God denies injustice so no one supposes that creating unbelief and then punishing the unbeliever is unjust; rejecting this account would attribute incapacity to God.
rows.anchor: ولهذا نفى الله -تعالى ذكره- الظلم عن نفسه كيلا يتوهم متوهم

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمؤرج وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Muʾarrij, and Abū ʿUbayda explain the comparison as the customary pattern of Pharaoh's people; the compared subject is omitted, meaning their pattern was like it.
rows.anchor: المشبه محذوف تقديره: دأبهم كدأب آل فرعون، قال الأخفش والمؤرج وأبو عبيدة:

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the present people's habit of disbelief matched Pharaoh's; they were repaid with killing and captivity as Pharaoh's people were repaid with drowning.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معناه: عادة هؤلاء في كفرهم كعادة آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʾb originally means sustained work or persistence and exertion; it came to mean a habit because a habit is something maintained regularly.
rows.anchor: وأصل الدأب في اللغة: إدامة العمل، يقال: فلان يدأب في كذا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say the people of Badr denied the truth as Pharaoh's people did and suffered a matching fate; Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh knew Moses was God's Prophet but rejected him, just as Muhammad's opponents rejected him, so God punished them for disbelief. The exposition was treated at Āl ʿImrān 3:11.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: يريد أن أهل بدر كذبوا كما كذب آل فرعون ونزل بهم كما نزل بآل فرعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās elaborates that Pharaoh's people knew he lied and Moses was God's Prophet but denied him; Muhammad's opponents likewise denied the truth and his prophethood, so God punished them as He had Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: هكذا كان دأب آل فرعون أيقنوا أن فرعون كذاب عاد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is strong means that He is capable and nothing can overcome Him.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {إن الله قوي} أي قادر لا يغلبه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is severe in punishment for those who disbelieve in Him and deny His messengers.
rows.anchor: {شديد العقاب} لمن كفر به وكذب رسله
